models.collectorNote: The 2023 Tribute Edition (1,000 cars) is the collector marker. Ordinary GTs are the used bargain of the class, check for the hatch rattle fix and diff service.

generations.name: Stinger GT
generations.note: The 3.3 V6 was the car; the 2.0 four was the fleet special. A hatchback boot and genuine 70/30 rear bias made it the thinking enthusiast's daily.

models.intro: Kia's gran turismo: rear-drive, a twin-turbo V6, and chassis tuning by BMW M's former engineering chief Albert Biermann. It never sold like a 4 Series, which is why the good ones are bargains.

generations.name: EV6 / EV6 GT
generations.note: 10–80% charging in about 18 minutes set the class standard. The GT added dual motors, an electronic diff, and drift mode without losing the family brief.

models.intro: The E-GMP skateboard in a shooting-brake suit: 800-volt charging, a European Car of the Year trophy, and a GT flagship with 576 hp that embarrassed supercars at drag strips.

generations.name: Telluride
generations.note: One engine, one brief: a 3.8 V6, eight seats, and an interior that embarrassed luxury brands. The X-Pro trim adds genuine off-road kit; a hybrid second generation follows mid-decade.

models.intro: The three-row that swept the 2020 awards, World Car of the Year, MotorTrend SUV of the Year, North American Utility of the Year, by being honest, handsome, and priced under the Germans it out-finished.

generations.name: Soul
generations.note: Peter Schreyer's 'tiger nose' era. Cheap, cheerful, and styled like nothing else at the price, the car that made Kia a design brand in the US.

generations.name: Soul
generations.note: The third car added a 201 hp turbo and the boxy EV variant abroad. US production ended after 2025 as Kia's line-up electrified around it.

models.intro: The box the hamsters sold: a tall hatchback with genuine design wit that became Kia's American breakthrough car. Three generations over 16 years before the market moved to crossovers proper.
